questions.question: In Python, an if statement executes its indented block only when the condition evaluates to True.
The else block in an if statement is optional in Python.
Python requires parentheses around the condition in an if statement.
In an if statement, the equality operator '==' can be replaced by '=' to check for equality.
If a Python if statement does not include an indented block after the condition, it results in an IndentationError.
In a nested if statement, the inner if condition is evaluated only if the outer if condition is True.
A one-line if statement like 'if x > 0: print("Positive")' is valid in Python.
When using multiple separate if statements (not chained with elif), if more than one condition is True, only the first block will execute.
Python's if statements support compound conditions using logical operators such as 'and' and 'or'.
In an if statement, the expression 'a and b or c' is evaluated as ((a and b) or c) due to the operator precedence in Python.
